items.prompt: Black to move (Advance Variation, after 6.Be3). Name a good move; several are close, and two were played far more often than the rest.

claims.statement: Qb6, cxd4, Ne7 and Bg4 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).

hints: Black's c-pawn attacks the base of White's chain. What can Black do to d4, or to the pawn behind it?
One move uses the queen to attack a pawn that no White piece guards; the other trades the c-pawn for the pawn on d4.
The queen goes to b6, or the c-pawn takes on d4; a knight or bishop developing move is also close.
items.explain: Qb6 attacks the pawn on b2, which nothing guards, and keeps the tension on d4. cxd4 trades Black's c-pawn for the base of the chain and opens the position. Ne7 and Bg4 are also within 0.4 pawns of the best move (depth 16). In our master games the queen move was played 174 times and the capture 145 times.

items.prompt: Black to move after 8.O-O. The queen could take the pawn on b2 (Qxb2), far from home. Is Qxb2 one of the engine's best moves, or clearly worse?

claims.statement: Qxb2 and c4 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).
The pawn on b2 is attacked by the queen and guarded by nothing.

hints: Which White piece guards the pawn on b2?
Count the guards of b2: bishop, queen, knight, rook.
Nothing guards it, so the grab does not lose the queen at once.
items.explain: Nothing guards b2: the queen takes it for free, and the question is only what it costs to leave the queen so far from home. The engine rates Qxb2 within a few hundredths of a pawn of its best move (depth 16), and all 87 master games that reached this position took the pawn.

items.prompt: The same position with one change: the white rook stands on b1, not a1. Is Qxb2 still one of the engine's best moves, or clearly worse?

claims.statement: Qxb2 is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
No White piece is loose: the rook guards b2.

hints: What changed on the b-file?
Which piece now guards b2?
The rook takes the queen.
items.explain: With the rook on b1 the pawn on b2 is guarded, so Qxb2 is met by Rxb2 and the queen is lost for a pawn. The pawn grab depends on b2 having no guard. That is the first thing to check, not the only one: later boards show what else decides it.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's queen has taken the pawn on b2. Find White's best reply.

claims.statement: Qe1 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
Nb5 is at least 40 centipawns worse than Qe1 (depth 16).

hints: White has no quick way to win the queen. What does White need before the queen can be hunted?
Think about which piece leaves the d-file and which line it eyes.
The queen steps to e1.
items.explain: The queen steps off the d-file to e1, which keeps the diagonal towards b4 and a5 in view and prepares rook and knight moves against the black queen. The engine puts Qe1 first and Nb5 at least 0.4 pawns behind it (depth 16): after Nb5 c4 the black queen gets air and the attack loses its sting.

feedback_by_move.c3b5: Nb5 c4 and the black queen gets air. The engine puts Nb5 at least 0.4 pawns behind Qe1 (depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on a4 attacks the queen on b2, and the queen on e1 attacks the bishop on a5. Find Black's best move.

claims.statement: Bxe1 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
Qd2 is at least 300 centipawns worse (depth 16).
Two Black pieces are loose: the queen on b2 and the bishop on a5.

hints: Two Black pieces are attacked. Can one move save both?
Which White piece attacks the bishop, and can the bishop capture it?
The bishop takes the queen on e1.
items.explain: The knight on a4 attacks the queen on b2 and the queen on e1 attacks the bishop on a5, and both Black pieces are loose. The bishop can take the white queen: Bxe1 trades queens, and the knight then takes the black queen. Anything else loses the queen for less (depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move (Advance Variation, White has castled instead of playing Be3). Find a good move.

claims.statement: Nc6 and Ne7 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).

hints: The break c5 is already played. What attacks d4 further?
Which knight develops with a threat to the base of the chain?
The knight from b8 goes to c6.
items.explain: The knight on c6 adds a second attacker to d4 and keeps the e-pawn in play for the recapture; the knight on e7 heads for the same plan from the kingside. Our master data shows 80 games with 6...Nc6 here.

items.prompt: White to move (Advance Variation, after 7...Ne7). Find a good move.

claims.statement: c4, Nd2, O-O, h4 and Nc3 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).

hints: Which White piece is still undeveloped on the queenside?
Is any break available to attack Black's centre pawn on d5?
Several natural moves keep White's edge: a knight development, castling, the c-pawn break or a rook-pawn push.
items.explain: The knight developments, castling, the c-pawn break that attacks d5 and the rook-pawn push that gains space on the kingside are all near the top (depth 16). In our master data castling was played in 78 games, Nd2 in 47 and c4 in 11: counts are results, not evaluations, and the most common move is not always the engine's first choice.
